# Points (particle set geometry)

UsdGeom point cloud, read by the runtime only as particle geometry: a Points [prim](glossary.md#prim) that lists PhysxParticleSetAPI becomes a PBD particle set seeded from its points and velocities. Points and [PointInstancer](glossary.md#pointinstancer) are the only particle-set targets a PhysxParticleSamplingAPI sampler accepts.

## Columns

*Raw fallback* is the [USD](glossary.md#usd) schema value. *Producer writes* is what [ovstage](glossary.md#ovstage) population puts in the column for a USD stage. *Parser default* applies on the consumer when the column is absent, in stage units. **diverges** means writing the raw fallback literally parses differently from omitting the column (the parser default): USD population may well publish that very value for an unauthored attribute, so the marker is about the column being present, not about its value.

| Column | Type | Units | Raw fallback | Producer writes | Parser default | If absent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `points` | float32[3] array, POINT | length |  | not written |  | An absent or empty column yields a particle set with no particles. Read only when the prim lists PhysxParticleSetAPI. |
| `velocities` | float32[3] array, VECTOR | length/s |  | not written |  | Zero initial velocity for every particle. A non-empty column whose length differs from points makes the runtime reject the set with the warning 'PhysxSchemaPhysxParticleSetAPI parsing failed'. |

## Interactions

- **[`PhysxParticleSetAPI`](PhysxParticleSetAPI.md):** Makes the prim a particle set; without it points and velocities are not read.
- **[`PhysxParticleSamplingAPI`](PhysxParticleSamplingAPI.md):** A sampler's physxParticleSampling:particles target must be a Points or PointInstancer prim that lists PhysxParticleSetAPI; otherwise the runtime warns that the sampler does not point to a valid particle prim and does not sample.
- **[`PhysxParticleAnisotropyAPI`](PhysxParticleAnisotropyAPI.md):** When the owning system has anisotropy enabled and no isosurface, creating a set on a Points prim warns that anisotropy cannot be rendered with UsdGeomPoints.

## Notes

- The runtime reads points and velocities the same way on any PointBased prim (a [Mesh](glossary.md#mesh), for example) that lists PhysxParticleSetAPI; only the sampler and its target check require a Points or PointInstancer prim.
- Particle sampling also reads and rewrites widths on a Points sampler target; it is not described here.
